criticisms.claim: The A4 and A5 builds reach outside testers with no line that the 'before an outside tester plays' gate list (X-02) is green on that commit, and no brief asks for a flash reading of a horde wave. A4 is the build that adds the horde (most bodies and effects on screen), two fights on one screen and new form looks.
criticisms.fix: Add 'X-02 (must pass) on this commit before the build is uploaded or sent' to the A4 and A5 exits; add a largest-horde-wave clip (both modes) to the standard clip set in Tools' A4 brief and a reading row for it to Legal's A4 brief.
criticisms.vnote: A2 and A3 exits carry the gate list; A4 and A5 exits do not, and A4/ep.md criterion 5 lists ten lines without X-02 while criterion 6 sends the build to the two friends. No A4 or A5 brief asks for a flash reading of a horde wave (flash checks there cover only the two-fights clips, the collapse clip and the transformation clip). Partial cover that exists: Legal's A4 criterion 2 holds the outside package until the two-fights clips pass and criterion 5 adds its rows to the gate list; Art's criterion 4 flash-checks the transformation clip; QA's A5 protocol stops a session on a gate not green but is not an exit line.
criticisms.fix_ok: Sound. Smaller: one standing line beside 04-path-to-alpha.md:39 (no build is uploaded or sent to an outside tester unless the X-02 list is green on that commit) covers A3 to A6 at once; keep the horde-wave clip in Tools' A4 brief and Legal's reading row.

criticisms.claim: The newcomer criteria (X-18, X-19) are never run on a newcomer, and X-01 has no spare tester: the same two friends install at A2, get updates at A3 and A4, and are then the 'real pass' at A6.
criticisms.fix: Ask Orb for four Deck owners: two for A2 to A4, two held back who first see the game at A6 and give the X-18/X-19 reading. If only two exist, say in the path that X-18 at A6 is a re-install by experienced testers and put that to Orb.
criticisms.vnote: Exactly two friends are recruited and the same two are used at A2, for the A3 and A4 updates, and as the 'real pass' at A6. The only reading on true newcomers is A2's, on a draft guide, which the path itself calls 'not a pass yet'. No decision asks for a third or held-back tester.
criticisms.fix_ok: Sound; the fallback (say plainly that A6's X-18 is a re-install by experienced testers and put that to the owner) is the smallest honest version if only two Deck owners exist.

criticisms.claim: No exit line says anything about known bugs: the candidate can pass X-01 to X-34 with any number of open severe bugs, and nothing inside the totals budgets fixing what Orb's own plays find at A1, A3, A4 and A5.
criticisms.fix: Add a criterion X-35: no open bug of the top severity on the candidate, and every open bug of the next severity seen by Orb and carried by name. Give A1, A3, A4 and A5 each a named fix reserve for Orb's play reports, inside the totals.
criticisms.vnote: No exit line reads the bug list; A-QA-07's criterion field is empty; A1 criterion 8 accepts 'open'; the only fix reserves are after the two tester rounds; the 25% rework sits outside the 201M. Intake is covered (A3, A4, A6 briefs log every problem with a severity) and path:446 forces newcomer-stopping tester findings to be fixed in-milestone, so the hole is the exit bar and the budget. One weak evidence point: specification line 203 covers lines of the definition, and the definition has no line on known bugs, so this is a recommended addition, not a breach.
criticisms.fix_ok: X-35 is sound. For the reserves, smaller: state that fixes from the owner's plays at A1, A3, A4 and A5 are paid from the 25% rework line and count that line in the weeks, instead of four new reserves.

criticisms.fix: One required row in A2 (Simulation with Tools): the same seeded match on the Windows and Linux exports gives the same gameplay hash, and a report made on Linux verifies on Windows; re-run at A6.

Also a Deck tester in solo, couch or horde leaves no match file today (SAVES.md:101), so 'every report will be replayed' assumes recording those modes do not have.
criticisms.fix_ok: Better: make A-TOOLS-13 required in A2 (its own cost basis is one Windows step that plays the bench and compares the hash) and add 'a replay saved on Linux verifies on Windows' to X-27's reading at A6.

Performance's A2 brief supplies the install and bench steps for the friends' sheet, QA drafts the sheet, and Controls' A2 criterion 5 writes a sourced page on how a hand-added game gets its controls on a Deck. A2 is designed as a first reading that tries both routes, with a failed start fixed in-milestone.
criticisms.fix_ok: Better: do the skipped look-up first and add one criterion to Performance's A2 brief (chosen route, where the two files land, how they are posted from the Deck, each step sourced); move the no-keyboard package work to A2 only if the look-up shows the itch app route does not work.

criticisms.claim: GW1 has no pass-or-fail test that main became the 9 November game: behaviour changes (meters zeroed, perfect-block fix, two beam input fixes) ride in the same window as the switch flip, and the golden record is made only after the window closes. While the eight switch groups land one at a time main has no valid golden record, so each group's 'own gate run' has nothing to compare against, and A1's claim that 'nothing is meant to be different' rests on stills and the owner's eye.
criticisms.fix: Split GW1. GW1a: record the golden first on the kept 9 November tree's packed data (the target), land switch groups only, close A-CODE-01 when main reproduces that golden bit for bit. GW1b, straight after and before the first desktop build: the four riders, then one re-record.
criticisms.vnote: GW1's list mixes the switch rows with A-ENERGY-05, A-AI-10, A-COMBAT-05 and A-COMBAT-11 (path:99), and the golden record is made only after A-CODE-01 closes (A1/simulation-engine.md criterion 5). Nothing says what a group's 'own gate run' compares against once the old golden (valid only with switches off, A-CODE-02) no longer fits. One overstatement: a pass-or-fail test of the data does exist (Tools' count of differing switch rows reaching 0, A1/ep.md criterion 2, plus reads of the first build's packed data). What is missing is any test of behaviour.
criticisms.fix_ok: Sound. A kept 9 November tree exists and already replays headless to a saved final hash (tools/feel/feel-selftest.mjs:1), so the target golden can be recorded on it. It costs one extra re-record, and it lets the owner's 9 November play files verify on main at the end of GW1a, which answers most of ORD-05.

criticisms.vnote: A3 has the re-run line (path:172). A4's and A5's exit lists have none, while A4/ep.md criterion 6 sends the build to the two Deck friends and A5 puts its build on the same channels (path:250). criticisms.vnote: Team and horde bands are first read after GW3 and 'reported, not tuned here' (A4/qa-balance.md criterion 1). GW4 lists only A-AI-02, A-QA-05, A-QA-08 (path:264), no A5 brief names a team or horde band, and A6 requires them to hold. criticisms.fix_ok: Sound. Team and horde numbers are data, so naming them in GW4 fits its values-only rule; the X-10 rewording is optional given Game Design's A4 criterion 3.

criticisms.claim: X-14 (three times the crater width at the top tier) must pass at A4, but the only row behind it (A-WORLD-06) closes in A3 as a measuring tool with tuning forbidden and a hash flag of false; no A4 brief, GW3 entry or owner question carries the change that would make it pass.
criticisms.fix: Before A3 starts, either add the tier energy change to GW2 as part of A-WORLD-06 (marked hash-changing, sized, with QA re-reading that a base-tier fight does not wreck the planet), or add X-14 to the proposed-changes table and the owner's A3 page as a question.
criticisms.vnote: True: no A4 brief owns X-14's pass, GW3 does not carry it, and X-14 is absent from the proposed-changes table although the area review recommended restating it (WORLD.md:100). Wrong in two places. (1) The 1.32 and 1.48 figures are for the energy model off; A-ENERGY-04 turns it on in GW1, and with it on the same send is about 3.5 times wider at top level by the register's own verify note (radius 356 to 1,244, power-scale.md:54), or about 2.7 by the area review's arithmetic, so A1 may already carry the pass. criticisms.fix_ok: A smaller fix is enough: add X-14 to the proposed-changes table with WORLD.md:100's wording as the fallback, say which two levels are compared, and state that the keep, restate or tune choice is made on A3's reading before GW2 closes. No new GW2 row is needed yet.

criticisms.claim: Checks that replay the owner's saved play files are scheduled at moments when the game's own rule refuses those files; A-NET-05 is deliberately landed before GW1, which adds a second refusal. X-17 keeps naming 'saved play files' at A3 and A6, after windows that void every file saved so far.
criticisms.fix: State in step 4 that the comparison clip is made on a scratch copy carrying the full 9 November data with only the landing group read from main; give Tools a written tools-only way to re-feed a foreign file's inputs unverified (never in a tester's build); reword X-17 from A3 on to 'the scripted set plus every play file saved on this build'; run A2's fault hunt (A-RENDER-02, A-RENDER-03) on the kept 9 November tree.
criticisms.vnote: True: a replay is refused on other data (replay.gd:135-136), the briefs ask for comparisons at the same ticks of a saved play file on main while its data differs and give no method, the GW1 riders mean the same inputs cannot give the same match for step 6, and X-17 keeps naming the saved play files after windows that void them. Wrong in two places. (1) A tools-only way to re-feed a saved match on changed data already exists: the feel replay patches a scratch copy of the kept tree and runs the whole match open loop (feel.mjs:6, feel.gd:2-5). (2) A2's fault hunt works as written, because Tools replays a file on the kept build of the file's own commit.
criticisms.fix_ok: Smaller fix: no new tool. One sentence in steps 4 and 6 naming the method (scratch copy of the kept tree with the landing group's data, or ORD-01's split so the files verify on main before the riders), and reword X-17 from A3 to 'the scripted set plus play files saved on this build'.

The 9-week low end of the total inherits the error.

The path prices a tester round at one to two weeks, so a 1-week low end cannot hold. The milestone low ends add up to 9.5 weeks, so the total's low end inherits it.
criticisms.fix_ok: Sound. Note that A3's Order waits on A2 being closed (A3/ep.md:40), so 'A3 proceeds during the tester round' is a real change to the plan and must be written into that Order line too.

lenses.looked_at: Read whole: 04-path-to-alpha.md; 02-areas/LEGAL.md (gate list G1 to G20); questions.md; 07-skipped.md; all six orb.md pages; the EP's briefs A1 to A4; Legal's briefs A1 to A4; Tools' briefs A1 and A2; Performance's, Production's, Community & Marketing's and Camera's A2 briefs; Narrative's and part of UI's A5 briefs. criticisms.claim: The A4 and A5 builds reach the two outside friends with no re-run of the 'before an outside tester plays' gates; only A3 has that line. Rehearse update and roll-back on a separate dummy channel. If the re-run is too dear, do not send A4 to the friends.
criticisms.vnote: Only A3 carries the re-run line (path:172, A3/ep.md:25, A3/tools-pipeline.md:30). A4's exit list and A4/ep.md:20 have no X-02 line, yet A4/ep.md:22 sends the build to the two friends; its one safety hold is Legal's two-fights row (A4/legal-ip.md:20, :23). criticisms.claim: A friend's own bench and report files are planned into the repository, which is public. The friend was told reports go to a private server and can be deleted on request; a committed file cannot be taken back, and 'names removed first' does not cover what the friend typed.
criticisms.fix: One rule in the A2 Legal, Performance, QA and EP briefs: a tester's raw file is never committed; it lives in a git-ignored folder (ignore line added in A1 with A-PROCESS-03) and only the team's own reading (numbers, no quoted notes) goes under docs/*/runs/. Add a delete step to Production's release page.
criticisms.vnote: A2/performance-platform.md:22 records 'both files' (a friend's bench file and report file) under docs/perf/runs/<sha>/deck/, a tracked folder in a repository the content screen calls public. The report ends with the tester's free notes (ui_feedback.gd:163-164) and the note promises deletion on request (alpha-tester-note.md:30). No brief keeps a tester's raw file out of git; LEGAL.md:35 keeps only the tester list out. A2/ep.md:19 itself only hands files on.
criticisms.fix_ok: Yes, the smallest sound fix: raw tester files in a git-ignored folder, only the team's own reading committed, plus a delete step. The one line that must change is A2/performance-platform.md:22; the same rule belongs in A6/qa-balance.md:16-17.

criticisms.claim: The plan has CI on a public repository make the game's Windows and Linux programs from A1, weeks before the flash gate is green and before Orb's recorded yes. The existing workflow treats run files as reachable by others. Legal is asked whether Orb's own builds may be made early, but not whether a public run may carry them, in what lock state, or how the build reaches Orb's PC. Off Orb's page.
criticisms.fix: Reword X-29 for A1: CI builds, checks and discards; no game program is kept as a run file until G4 is green and the approval exists; Orb's A1 copy is made on Orb's PC by the same one command. Add to A1/legal-ip.md criterion 2: say whether any CI run on the public repository may keep a game program, locked or not.
criticisms.vnote: True: X-29 must pass at A1 with a CI run making both builds (path:70, A1/tools-pipeline.md:33) before G4 is green (LEGAL.md:23, closing in A2) and before the recorded yes; the workflow keeps game programs as run files for a day and relies on the EP deleting the run. How the build reaches Orb's PC is unstated. Wrong in part: A1/legal-ip.md:20 does ask Legal 'what the workflow must still refuse' and for 'the exact condition Tools should code', which leaves room for the lock state and the run-file question; it just does not name them. The plan also follows the specification's own evidence line for X-29 (spec:196).
criticisms.fix_ok: Rewording X-29 is more than needed and departs from the specification's line. Smaller: add to A1/legal-ip.md criterion 2 that the ruling must say whether a run on the public repository may keep a game program, in what lock state and for how long, and how Orb's copy reaches Orb's PC; Tools codes that condition and keeps no run file until the ruling exists.

criticisms.claim: The approval step cannot be followed as written. Orb's yes is to be recorded only after every gate is green, but four gates' records come from the package step, and the workflow refuses to build a tester package until the approval file is committed in the commit being built. The approval also expires after 30 days, and A2's yes is five to eleven weeks old by A6. The likely way out is the EP recording the yes early.
criticisms.fix: In Legal's A2 ruling (A-TOOLS-06, A2/legal-ip.md:23) split the two acts: 'may build and check a tester package, hand to nobody' (no approval) and 'may hand out commit <sha>' (Orb's yes, checked at the upload step). Put a re-approval line on Orb's A3 to A6 pages, or have the ruling say one yes covers named commits.
criticisms.vnote: The loop is real: G8 (the approval file in the candidate commit, LEGAL.md:27) sits on the list that must be green before the approval is recorded (A2/ep.md:16); G6, G7 and G9 are recorded from the package's routes and verify output; the workflow refuses to build without the committed file (yml:56) and A1/tools-pipeline.md:33 keeps the tester package refused until then. Committing the file also makes a new commit after the gates were read. Wrong in part: freshness is already put to Legal ('how fresh Orb's approval must be', A2/legal-ip.md:23) and A6 records the approval again (A6/legal-ip.md:16). 'The EP records it early' is a guess with no evidence.
criticisms.fix_ok: The split is the right fix and the smallest: 'build and check a tester package, hand to nobody' needs no approval; 'hand out commit <sha>' needs Orb's yes, checked at the upload step. The re-approval line for A3 to A5 can be left to the freshness answer Legal already owes in A2/legal-ip.md:23.

criticisms.claim: The flash gate reads the browser export; the friends get the Linux desktop program on a 1280 by 800 Deck screen at a Deck quality level. Nothing proves the two draw the same picture over the measured clips, and the path itself expects desktop-against-browser differences. Off Orb's page.
criticisms.fix: Add one line to G4 in Legal's gate page (A-LEGAL-03): the desktop Linux build's frames match the browser build's over the standard clips' tick windows, at 1280 by 800 and at the Deck's default level, compared in CI under the virtual display from spike S5; a mismatch makes G4 red. Owner: Tools with Rendering.
criticisms.vnote: The pass is keyed to the Web preset and a Windows or Linux preset change leaves it alone (release-pass.mjs:10); no register row or brief reads the flash clips on a desktop program. Partial cover exists: A1 compares each desktop build with the browser build by stills at the same ticks of one replay (path:55) and S5 saves one Linux still (path:63). Neither covers the standard clips, 1280 by 800 or the Deck's level.
criticisms.fix_ok: The aim is right but a frame-for-frame match between a desktop driver and a browser is too strict and will fail on harmless differences. Better: run the analyser itself on the Linux desktop build's frames for the standard clips (the desktop capture hook from A2/tools-pipeline.md:39, in CI under S5's virtual display, 1280 by 800, Deck default level) and hold them to the same limits; G4 is red if that reading is missing or over.

Ask Orb question 15 only after the ruling is written.

(path:497), A2's rehearsal needs the ruling landed (A2/tools-pipeline.md:53), and the search is a spend left to Orb (A1/legal-ip.md:26). criticisms.fix_ok: Keep only the first half: one line in A1/legal-ip.md criterion 1 and decision 9 saying what happens on a 'no' (a neutral placeholder name Legal screens in the same row, or the search brought forward as a spend question to Orb). The reordering of question 15 is not needed.

criticisms.fix_ok: Yes: say the forced crash lives in CI (A2/tools-pipeline.md:32 already has that test) and in Orb's own unlocked copy, and strike it from the itch.io install step at path:115 and A2/orb.md:14.
